prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
During the third quarter of 2026, we recorded a provision for credit losses of $16.1 million, compared to $13.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. The provision for credit losses in the third quarter of 2026 included net charge-offs of $10.2 million and a reserve build of $5.9 million, including $1.0 million attributable to a provision for unfunded commitments assumed in the acquisition of OFB, identified as a supplemental disclosure item. The provision for credit losses in the second quarter of 2026 included net charge-offs of $9.4 million and a reserve build of $4.4 million. The provision for credit losses in both periods reflect mostly stable credit quality and modest builds attributable to loan growth.

Annualized net charge-offs as a percentage of average loans in the third quarter of 2026 were 0.16%, unchanged from the second quarter of 2026. Net charge-offs in the third quarter of 2026 included $7.3 million in the commercial portfolio, $2.5 million in the consumer portfolio and $0.4 million in the residential mortgage portfolio.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text: Noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2026 was $262.0 million, up $36.6 million, or 16%, from the second quarter of 2026. Included in the three months ended September 30, 2026 were supplemental disclosure items totaling $29.4 million related to the acquisition of OFB Bancshares, Inc. Excluding the supplemental disclosure items, noninterest expense was up $7.2 million, or 3%, from the second quarter of 2026, driven largely by increases in personnel, and occupancy and equipment expense. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense totaled $708.2 million, up $74.4 million, or 12%, from the same period in 2025. Included in noninterest expense for nine months ended September 30, 2026 were the $29.4 million of OFB acquisition-related supplemental disclosure items mentioned above. Included in the nine months ended September 30, 2025 were supplemental disclosure items totaling $5.9 million attributable to the Sabal acquisition. Excluding the supplemental disclosure items in each respective period, noninterest expense was up $51.0 million, or 8%, from the same period in 2025, with increases across most categories but largely driven by increases in personnel, business development, and data processing expenses. A more detailed discussion of noninterest expense variances follows.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 22.5%, compared to 21.7% in the second quarter of 2026. The linked-quarter increase in the effective tax rate was due primarily to increased nondeductible expenses attributable to the OFB acquisition that closed in the third quarter of 2026. The effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 21.6%, compared to 20.6% for the same period in 2025.

Many factors impact the effective income tax rate including, but not limited to, the level of pre-tax income and relative impact of net tax benefits related to tax credit investments, tax-exempt interest income, bank-owned life insurance, and nondeductible expenses. Additionally, discrete tax items recognized in any given period affect the comparability of the effective income tax rate between periods. Such items include share-based compensation, valuation allowance changes, uncertain tax position changes and tax law changes.

Our effective tax rate has historically varied from the federal statutory rate primarily because of tax-exempt income and tax credits. Interest income on bonds issued by or loans to state and municipal governments and authorities, and earnings from the bank-owned life insurance program are the major components of tax-exempt income.

net.text: We define Adjusted Pre-Provision Net Revenue as net income excluding provision expense and income tax expense, plus the taxable equivalent adjustment (as defined above), less supplemental disclosure items (as defined above). Management believes that adjusted pre-provision net revenue is a useful financial measure because it enables investors and others to assess the Company’s ability to generate capital to cover credit losses through a credit cycle. We define Adjusted Revenue as net interest income (te) and noninterest income less supplemental disclosure items. We define Adjusted Noninterest Expense as noninterest expense less supplemental disclosure items. We define our Efficiency Ratio as noninterest expense to total net interest income (te) and noninterest income, excluding amortization of purchased intangibles and supplemental disclosure items, if applicable. Management believes adjusted revenue, adjusted noninterest expense and the efficiency ratio are useful measures as they provide a greater understanding of ongoing operations and enhance comparability with prior periods.

da.text: Occupancy and equipment expenses are primarily composed of lease expenses, depreciation, maintenance and repairs, rent, property taxes, and other equipment expenses. Occupancy and equipment expenses totaled $20.1 million for the third quarter of 2026, up $1.8 million, or 10%, from the second quarter of 2026, primarily attributable to increases in equipment expense, building repair and maintenance, utilities and leased facility expense. sbc.text: The tangible common equity (TCE) ratio was 8.05% at September 30, 2026, down 201 bps from 10.06% at December 31, 2025, driven by the impact of the OFB acquisition (-114 bps), other comprehensive loss (-52 bps), common stock repurchases (-64 bps), dividends (-36 bps) and tangible asset growth (-23 bps), partially offset by tangible net earnings (+85 bps) and stock-based compensation and other (+3 bps).

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income (te) for the third quarter of 2026 totaled $314.9 million, up $19.7 million, or 7%, from the second quarter of 2026, and $897.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, up $63.2 million, or 8%, from the same period in 2025.

The $19.7 million increase in net interest income (te) from the second quarter of 2026 is comprised of an increase in interest income (te) of $33.5 million that was partially offset by an increase in interest expense of $13.8 million. The acquisition of OFB contributed approximately $22.8 million of interest income, inclusive of $3.3 million of accretion of the fair value discount, and $7.9 million of interest expense. Outside of the contributions from the OFB acquisition, the increase in interest income (te) was driven primarily by increases in yields on securities and loans, organic loan growth and the impact of an additional accrual day. The increase in interest expense from our legacy operation was driven primarily by increases in the average balance and cost of interest-bearing deposits and the impact of an additional accrual day, partially offset by a decrease in average short-term borrowings. Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income totaled $107.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, down $1.3 million, or 1%, from the second quarter of 2026, driven primarily by declines in secondary mortgage market operations, trust fees and investment and annuity fees, partially offset by increases in service charges on deposits and other miscellaneous income. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest income totaled $222.8 million, down $76.5 million from the same period in 2025. Included in noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was a $98.6 million loss identified as a supplemental disclosure item attributable to the restructuring of the available for sales securities portfolio. Excluding the supplemental disclosure item, noninterest income was up $22.1 million, or 7%, from the same period in 2025, with increases across most lines. intro.text: Hancock Whitney Corporation (the “Company”) is registered with the Federal Reserve as a bank holding company and has elected to be treated as a financial holding company under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. The Company provides comprehensive financial services through its bank subsidiary, Hancock Whitney Bank (the “Bank”), a Mississippi state bank, and other nonbank affiliates. Our principal executive offices are located at 2510 14 th Street, Gulfport, Mississippi, 39501, and our telephone number is (800) 522-6542. Our common stock trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol “HWC.”
